fields.name: PRECIPITATION

fields.name: WIND_DIRECTION_DEGREES

fields.name: ADJUSTED_WIND_SPEED

fields.name: DAILY_SEVERITY_RATING
fields.description: Daily Severity Rating is a numeric rating describing the difficulty of controlling fires. It is calculated from the Initial Spread Index and Build Up Index.

fields.name: DROUGHT_CODE
fields.description: Drought Code is a numerical rating of the moisture content of deep, compact, organic layers. It is a useful indicator of seasonal drought and shows the likelihood of fire involving the deep duff layers and large logs. A long period of dry weather (the system uses 52 days) is needed to dry out these fuels and affect the Drought Code. A DC rating of 200 is high, and 300 or more is extreme indicating that fire will involve deep sub-surface and heavy fuels. Burning off should not be permitted when the DC rating is above 300. Note: Drought Code is a meteorological business term and is not a true code that is looked up in a code table.

fields.name: DUFF_MOISTURE_CODE
fields.description: Duff Moisture Code is a numerical rating of the average moisture content of loosely compacted organic layers of moderate depth. The code indicates the depth that fire will burn in moderate duff layers and medium size woody material. Duff layers take longer than surface fuels to dry out but weather conditions over the past couple of weeks will significantly affect the DMC. The system applies a time lag of 12 days to calculate the DMC. A DMC rating of more than 30 is dry, and above 40 indicates that intensive burning will occur in the duff and medium fuels. Burning off operations should not be carried out when the DMC rating is above 40. Note: Duff Moisture Code is a meteorological business term and is not a true code that is looked up in a code table.

fields.name: FINE_FUEL_MOISTURE_CODE
fields.description: Fine Fuel Moisture Code (FFMC) is a measure of the moisture content (dryness) of the smallest forest fuels (surface litter, leaves, needles, small twigs, etc). It shows the relative ease of ignition and flammability of fine fuels. The moisture content of the fine fuels is very sensitive to the weather. Even a day of rain, or of fine and windy weather, will significantly affect the FFMC rating. Measured values translate as: 0-76 : Low 77-84: Moderate 85-88: High 89-91: Very High 92+: Extreme

fields.name: GRASSLAND_CURING
fields.description: Grassland Curing is a numeric rating of the state of the grassland moisture levels.

fields.name: BUILD_UP_INDEX
fields.description: Build Up Index shows the amount of fuel available for combustion, indicating how the fire will develope after initial spread. It is calculated from the Duff Moisture Code and Drought Code. The BUI Scale starts at 0 and is open-ended. A rating above 40 is high, and above 60 is extreme.

fields.name: DANGER_FOREST_INDEX
fields.description: Danger Forest Index is an index calculation specific to BC that is based on location Build Up Index and Fire Weather Index. Values fall in the range of 1-5.

fields.name: DANGER_GRASSLAND_INDEX
fields.description: Danger Grassland Index is an index calculation specific to BC that is based on location Initial Spread Index and Grass Curing. Values fall in the range of 1-5.

fields.name: DANGER_SCRUB_INDEX
fields.description: Danger Scrub Index is an index calculation specific to BC that is based on location Initial Spread Index and Fine Fuel Moisture Code. Values fall in the range of 1-5.

fields.name: FIRE_WEATHER_INDEX
fields.description: Fire Weather Index is calculated from the Initial Spread Index and a measure called BUI (Build-Up Index), and provides a numerical rating of the likely intensity of a fire. Values are: 0-4.5 : Low 4.5-10.5: Moderate 10.5-18.5: High 18.5-29.5: Very High 29.5+: Extreme

fields.name: INITIAL_SPREAD_INDEX
fields.description: Initial Spread Index indicates the rate fire will spread in its early stages. It is calculated from the FFMC rating and the wind factor. A high rating indicates a high rate of spread. Measured values translate as: 0-1.5 : Low 2-4: Moderate 5-8: High 9-15: Very High 16+: Extreme

fields.name: MISSING_HOURLY_DATA_IND

This field references whether the roll up values (Precipitation, Temperature_max/min, RH max/min) might be based on incomplete data. IE if hourly data is missing from 4am to 7am then the precipitation measurement may be missing some precipitation that occurred during that window.

fields.name: BAROMETRIC_PRESSURE
fields.description: Barometric Pressure is a measure of barometric pressure by the weather station. Atmospheric pressure, sometimes also called barometric pressure (after the sensor), is the pressure within the atmosphere of Earth (or that of another planet). The standard atmosphere (symbol: atm) is a unit of pressure defined as 1013.25 mbar (101325 Pa), equivalent to 760 mm Hg (torr), 29.9212 inches Hg, or 14.696 psi.[1] The atm unit is roughly equivalent to the mean sea-level atmospheric pressure on Earth, that is, the Earth's atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately 1 atm. In most circumstances atmospheric pressure is closely approximated by the hydrostatic pressure caused by the weight of air above the measurement point. As elevation increases, there is less overlying atmospheric mass, so that atmospheric pressure decreases with increasing elevation. Pressure measures force per unit area, with SI units of Pascals (1 pascal = 1 newton per square metre, 1 N/m2).

fields.name: WEATHER_STATION_GUID
fields.description: WEATHER_STATION_GUID: Is a foreign key to WEATHER_STATION: Weather Station is a list of weather stations setup and maintained across the province of BC. The weather stations contain multiple instruments for measuring varying aspects of meteorology used to produce weather forecasts.

fields.name: PERIOD_START_DATE
fields.description: Period Start Date is the date that the period start on.

fields.name: PERIOD_END_DATE
fields.description: Period End Date is the date the period ends on. Typically the period end date will be October 31st for the given year.

fields.name: ACTIVE_IND
fields.description: Active Ind indicates whether the defined station indices period is active (Y) or not (N). This allows a period to be disabled or allows for future period to be planned.

fields.name: FINE_FUEL_MOISTURE_CODE
fields.description: Fine Fuel Moisture Code (FFMC) is a measure of the moisture content (dryness) of the smallest forest fuels (surface litter, leaves, needles, small twigs, etc). It shows the relative ease of ignition and flammability of fine fuels. The moisture content of the fine fuels is very sensitive to the weather. Even a day of rain, or of fine and windy weather, will significantly affect the FFMC rating. Measured values translate as: 0-76 : Low 77-84: Moderate 85-88: High 89-91: Very High 92+: Extreme

fields.name: DROUGHT_CODE
fields.description: Drought Code is a numerical rating of the moisture content of deep, compact, organic layers. It is a useful indicator of seasonal drought and shows the likelihood of fire involving the deep duff layers and large logs. A long period of dry weather (the system uses 52 days) is needed to dry out these fuels and affect the Drought Code. A DC rating of 200 is high, and 300 or more is extreme indicating that fire will involve deep sub-surface and heavy fuels. Burning off should not be permitted when the DC rating is above 300. Note: Drought Code is a meteorological business term and is not a true code that is looked up in a code table.

fields.name: DUFF_MOISTURE_CODE
fields.description: Duff Moisture Code is a numerical rating of the average moisture content of loosely compacted organic layers of moderate depth. The code indicates the depth that fire will burn in moderate duff layers and medium size woody material. Duff layers take longer than surface fuels to dry out but weather conditions over the past couple of weeks will significantly affect the DMC. The system applies a time lag of 12 days to calculate the DMC. A DMC rating of more than 30 is dry, and above 40 indicates that intensive burning will occur in the duff and medium fuels. Burning off operations should not be carried out when the DMC rating is above 40. Note: Duff Moisture Code is a meteorological business term and is not a true code that is looked up in a code table.

fields.name: DAILY_MEASUREMENT_TYPE_CODE
fields.description: DAILY_MEASUREMENT_TYPE_CODE: Measurement Type Code describes the types of measurements that can be collected. It correlates to the original Data Status Code in the old system. Values are: - Actual - Forecast - Estimate - Edited Actual - Test - Startup - Deleted - Manual - Substitution - missing - Substitution - invalid - Substitution - partial
